subject: gov.policy
name: BCEAO regulatory approach to cryptoassets
milestone: C-CRYPTO committee established and an international conference held, May 2026
position_start: No recognition of cryptoassets as legal tender and repeated warnings to users, with no regulatory work under way
position_end: The central bank opened a structured process across 2025 and 2026: a questionnaire sent to fintech operators, a dedicated committee named C-CRYPTO, and a high-level international conference in May 2026. Cryptoassets remain outside legal tender and no instrument has been issued; the legal framework is described as still incomplete, and the question the bank has set itself is how to admit the instruments without compromising monetary stability, the issuance monopoly of the CFA franc and the integrity of the regional financial system
note: the account is a legal academic's analysis published in a trade outlet, not a central-bank statement; the questionnaire, the committee's membership and terms, and any conference output are not held

subject: gov.policy
name: ECOWAS Digital Sector Development Strategy 2024-2029
milestone: Adopted at the 19th ministerial meeting, Cotonou, 2024-10-04
position_end: Still unpublished, so its targets, budget and implementation arrangements are unestablished; the roaming implementation progress report and the directive on cyber confidence-building measures adopted alongside it are unpublished too
note: The Commission's own release is the only record of the adoption

subject: gov.policy
name: ECOWAS Regional Digital Single Market roadmap
milestone: Adopted at the Lagos thematic dialogue, 2026-01-22
position_end: Adopted as a commitment to harmonise policy across interoperable fintech, unified digital ID and rural broadband; no work programme, timetable or budget held
sources: 2026-01-24 ECOWAS Adopts Digital Roadmap; Targets Unified Single Market and AI Governance for West Africa

subject: gov.policy
name: WATRA technical reports on 5G, submarine-cable resilience, cybersecurity, consumer protection and NGSO
milestone: Finalised at the working-group meeting, Ouagadougou, 2026-04-02
position_end: Seven documents published: the cybersecurity working group's final report, the infrastructure working group's 2023-2025 report covering 5G, NGSO, cable resilience and WRC-27, the 5G deployment and policy framework, the submarine-cable resilience recommendations, the consumer access and experience regulatory synthesis and two of its seven constituent guidelines
note: Published under the 23rd General Assembly reference series; the cybersecurity report is marked final for adoption, so adoption is not established, and five of the seven consumer guidelines are not published individually

subject: gov.legislate
name: Cybercrime statutes in the Sahel states
milestone: Press-freedom body reported the pattern 2026-08-14
position_end: A press-freedom organisation reports the cybercrime statutes of Burkina Faso, Mali, Niger and Guinea being used to prosecute journalists, and calls for the repeal of vague public-order and human-dignity provisions
note: the finding is one organisation's, presented at a press-freedom conference; no government response and no case count are held

subject: gov.legislate
name: ECOWAS Supplementary Act A/SA.2/01/10 on Electronic Transactions
milestone: Adopted at the Thirty-Seventh Session of the Authority of Heads of State and Government, Abuja, 16 February 2010
position_end: The community's own act on electronic transactions, adopted alongside the companion act on personal-data protection this ledger holds separately; the full text is now held
note: Acquired to resolve a link the community's own listing page did not expose.

subject: gov.protect
name: ECOWAS Supplementary Act on the Protection of Personal Data
milestone: Adopted by the Authority of Heads of State and Government, Abuja, 16 February 2010
position_start: The Supplementary Act of February 2010, the regional benchmark national bills were still being drafted against
position_end: A revised Act adopted; its text is not published with the communique, so what changed against 2010 is not establishable from the base; the complete text is now held, adopted at the thirty-seventh session of the Authority of Heads of State and Government in Abuja on 16 February 2010
note: The 2010 Act is not itself held; it is known through the communique that supersedes it

subject: gov.regional
name: Alliance of Sahel States (AES)
milestone: Niger's prime minister enrolled for the AES passport, 2026-07-16
position_start: A common biometric passport launched in January 2025; harmonised document specifications validated but unpublished; no confederal card issued
position_end: Both confederal credentials issuing, a cross-border enrolment run on another member's soil, and a national data centre offered as mutualised AES infrastructure

subject: gov.regional
name: BCEAO (Banque Centrale des Etats de l'Afrique de l'Ouest)
milestone: Banking commission annual report published 2026-08-27
position_start: Operating the SICA and STAR systems, with the instant-payment platform in test phase
position_end: Operating the union's instant-payment rail, participating in the ECOWAS payment project and preparing a pilot accession to the continental one

subject: gov.regional
name: Cotonou Declaration on digital transformation in West and Central Africa
milestone: Adopted at the close of the Cotonou summit, 2025-11-18
position_end: Adopted by West and Central African states, committing to a single digital market by 2030; no implementation report, work plan or secretariat held in the nine months since

subject: gov.regional
name: Draft Directive Governing Electronic Communications in West Africa
milestone: Validation workshop, Abuja, 22-24 September 2025
position_end: A three-day validation workshop advanced the draft directive toward ministerial approval; no adopted text, ministerial date or transposition deadline is published

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS
milestone: New commission president took office 2026-08-31
position_start: Vision 2050 in force; the Supplementary Act of February 2010 the newest regional digital instrument the base held
position_end: a new president of the commission in office from 31 August 2026

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS project-preparation pipeline for digital connectivity
milestone: Commission directed to prioritise digital connectivity and report annually, 2026-07-19
position_end: Digital connectivity placed alongside transport, energy and water in the pipeline for development finance and private investment; no project list, envelope or first report held

subject: gov.regional
name: ECOWAS regional postal-sector regulatory framework
milestone: Revised Directive and master-plan outline endorsed by experts, Lome, 12-13 August 2026
position_start: The 2016 postal-sector Directive in force, with no revision on record
position_end: Officials from ten member states, meeting the Commission's digital economy and post directorate with the regional infrastructure preparation unit, the Pan-African Postal Union and the West African postal operators' body at Lome on 12-13 August 2026, validated the orientations of a revised Directive and the outline of a Regional Postal Master Plan 2027-2030, naming digital transformation, e-commerce, universal-service modernisation, consumer protection and financial inclusion as priority areas; consultations with member states on the revised Directive continue and neither text is published
note: an expert validation rather than an adoption; no adoption date, financing or text is published

subject: gov.regional
name: Praia framework and action plan on information integrity
milestone: Adopted at Praia, 5 September 2025
position_start: No regional instrument on information integrity (2025-08)
position_end: A twenty-page model policy framework and a ten-year action plan for 2026-2036 were adopted at the Praia ministerial conference, operationalised across four domains with outcomes and indicators, and reported in July 2026 as committing fifteen West African states to information-integrity laws (2026-07)

subject: gov.regional
name: UEMOA land registration harmonisation directive
milestone: Draft approved by eight member states, June 2026
position_start: No regional rule on land registration (2025-08)
position_end: Eight member states approved a draft directive harmonising land registration and titling rules across the union in June 2026, covering the establishment of urban land information systems; no domestic transposition is recorded (2026-06)

subject: gov.regional
name: WATRA (West Africa Telecommunications Regulators Assembly)
milestone: Fourth working-groups meeting concluded, Ouagadougou, 2026-04-12
position_start: Working groups established about two years earlier, with no technical output on record
position_end: Five technical reports finalised, a 23rd general assembly held at Lome, and a regional position stated on submarine-cable resilience
sources: 2026-04-13 WATRA rallies Africa for region's $216b digital economy|2026-07-15-watra-regional-subsea-resilience-plan|2026-07-24-watra-aboki-institutions-digital-investment|2026-04-21-artao-ppp-haut-debit
note: Sixteen member regulators, spanning ECOWAS states, the AES states and Mauritania

subject: gov.standards
name: AES harmonised specifications for travel and identity documents
milestone: Validated by the three security ministers at Bamako, 2024-11-22
position_start: Validated and referred to the heads of state; no approval, gazetted text or reference number
position_end: Unchanged, while both credentials built on them are issued; no published text located

subject: gov.standards
name: Alliance ouest-africaine des noms de domaine (AOAN)
milestone: Founding case put at the SIPEN-UEMOA salon, Ouagadougou, 2026-07-15
position_end: Announced as an initiative to coordinate country-code domain policy across the region; no charter, membership or founding act held
note: Convened by practitioners rather than by the registries or a regional body

subject: gov.standards
name: ECOWAS free-roaming regulation C/REG.21/12/17
milestone: Senegal, Togo and Benin arrangement took effect at Lome, 2026-04-24
movement: Advanced, against a missed end-2025 deadline
position_start: In force since December 2017, implemented between Liberia, The Gambia and Sierra Leone (2025-02), with full implementation by all mobile operators due by end-2025
position_end: A second three-state arrangement live, giving free incoming calls for up to 30 days and local rates on outgoing traffic; the end-2025 deadline passed with six of fifteen member states covered
note: The deadline was set by the ministers at Cotonou on 2024-10-04

subject: gov.standards
name: National accounting councils required of member states
milestone: Required by directive since 28 November 1997
position_start: The obligation standing with the newest member state's council not established
position_end: In force since 1997 and requiring each member state to establish a national accounting council; one member state launched its own in August 2026, twenty-nine years on
note: The base holds no roster of which member states have established theirs

subject: gov.standards
name: Regional certified electronic signature
milestone: Programme set out by the Commission, April 2024
position_end: The Commission has set out a programme towards a certified electronic signature usable across West Africa; no standard, root authority or member-state adoption is on file

subject: gov.discourse
name: Regional Feminist Data Agenda 2026-2028
milestone: Ratified at the close of the West Africa Feminist Data Summit, Porto-Novo, 2026-07-30
position_end: Ratified with three priorities for 2026-2028, each carrying a named owner, alongside eight thematic policy briefs and a cross-border encrypted data collective with rapid-response protocols; no text is published
note: The organiser's own account of its own summit; the delegate and country counts are RFLD's figures

subject: finance.budget
name: ECOWAS Community Budget provision for digital programmes
status: Discontinued, the only ICT programme line carries nil from 2024
milestone: No appropriation line found, Community Budget 2026-2028
position_start: No disaggregated digital or ICT line, and nil actual on the Youth Entrepreneurship in ICT line since 2023
position_end: The 2026-2028 MTEF carries no disaggregated digital or ICT line; Youth Entrepreneurship in ICT is nil from 2024 through the 2028 estimates, against UA 543,953 approved and UA 407,965 actual in 2022
note: Prepared on an IPSAS accrual basis with figures year-to-date at 2025-10-31; the nil runs from the 2024 financial year

subject: finance.new
name: Africa Connect Digital Campus
milestone: Project running October 2025 to April 2029
position_end: A EUR 4.2m European Union and French foreign ministry project to upgrade broadband connectivity, e-learning and national research and education networks at universities in Benin, Cote d'Ivoire and Togo under the Global Gateway strategy; no university list, bandwidth target or delivery milestone is published
note: Distinct from the budget-support programme running alongside it.

subject: finance.new
name: Co-investment in Coris Bank International
milestone: Co-investment announced 29 October 2025
position_end: A EUR 100m co-investment led by a private equity manager alongside four development finance institutions into the union's second-largest banking group; the amount is not broken out by country and no digital or financial-inclusion use of proceeds is stated

subject: finance.new
name: Digital Transformation Fund (BOAD/KfW)
milestone: Programme site published with eligibility terms and national focal points
position_end: A joint fund of the West African Development Bank and the German development bank carrying an envelope of 71 billion FCFA for digital modernisation of public administrations across the eight monetary-union states, with a published six-step instruction and validation process, a named focal point in each member state, and eligibility terms of a maximum 24-month project, a budget ceiling of 2,500 million FCFA, an interest rate the fund states at 2.2% and obligatory partial state co-financing; no date of signature or entry into force, no country allocation and no committed or disbursed total is published
note: the fund's own site puts the interest rate at 2.2% where a trade-press account of 2026-08-19 reports 2.77%; the first-party figure is carried here and the two are not reconciled. The site is undated and its publication date is the date it was read

subject: finance.new
name: Pooled equity investment in a pan-African start-up fund
milestone: Approved toward the fund's first close, 2026-08-09
position_end: EUR10.5m approved toward first close - EUR7m from the continental development bank and EUR3.5m from the European Union with the African, Caribbean and Pacific states - into a fund investing in agribusiness, financial services, energy, education and health, mainly in Francophone West Africa
note: made under the Boost Africa programme with the European Investment Bank; the European share is stated jointly with the Pacific-states contribution and is not separately disclosed

subject: finance.new
name: WARDIP (Western Africa Regional Digital Integration Program)
milestone: Liberia's financing agreement signed, 2026-06-08
position_start: The first series alone: US$293.00m across four states, ECOWAS, the African Union and Smart Africa
position_end: A second series approved on 2026-03-11 for Benin, Liberia and Sierra Leone, with Liberia's US$50m share signed in June
note: The largest single financing instrument the regional layer holds

subject: finance.new
name: World Bank commitment to the WARDIP series
position_end: US$430.00m across the two series, after US$137.00m was approved on 2026-03-11
note: Two separate operations; the total is their sum

subject: infra.connect
name: Community roaming regulation implementation
milestone: Three states entered the free roaming agreement, February 2026
position_start: Compliance with the 2017 roaming regulation reviewed by national regulators, with tariff compliance uneven (2025-08)
position_end: Liberia, Ghana and Sierra Leone formally entered the free roaming agreement in February 2026, removing roaming charges among the three, with the regulator stressing that full implementation still had to follow (2026-02)

subject: infra.connect
name: CSquared West Africa backbone

position_end: Capacity on the 2Africa West system added for route diversity, after three multi-country outages in 28 months at the Accra, Lagos and Abidjan landing concentration
sources: 2026-07-15 CSquared boosts internet by integrating with 2Africa West cable

subject: infra.connect
name: ECOWAS second submarine cable (Cabo Verde, Liberia, Sierra Leone, Guinea-Bissau)
milestone: Feasibility study reviewed and approved at the expert workshop, Monrovia, 22-24 October 2025
position_end: Member-state experts with technical and financial partners reviewed and approved the feasibility study for a second submarine cable serving four member states, at a workshop organised by the community's project preparation and development unit; the stated aims are better integration of Cabo Verde with the region, more international capacity and route redundancy, and no route, cost, landing site or construction date is published
note: The same record sits on the four member states' own ledgers.

subject: infra.connect
name: EllaLink Mauritania branch
milestone: First-phase coastal landing completed, 2026-05-04
position_start: Launched at Nouadhibou in July 2025, with nothing laid

note: Mauritania's second international cable and its first redundancy against the ACE system

subject: infra.connect
name: Nigeria-Burkina Faso connectivity partnership
milestone: Discussed at a ministerial visit to Ouagadougou, 2026-08-13
position_end: Technical teams to assess routes through Niger and through Benin, on a stated aim of halving the cost of internet access in Burkina Faso
note: an exploratory discussion under Nigeria's Project BRIDGE; no agreement, route, cost or date is settled, and the 50% is a stated aim

subject: infra.connect
name: Second submarine cable bid evaluation
milestone: Bids evaluated at Abuja, 29 June to 10 July 2026
position_start: A second submarine cable planned across five member states (2025-10)
position_end: An evaluation committee spanning the five participating states met at Abuja from 29 June to 10 July 2026 to assess bids for the cable's capacity (2026-07)

subject: infra.connect
name: Via Africa submarine cable
milestone: Memorandum of understanding signed, 2026-05-13
position_end: A consortium memorandum signed by Canalink, GUILAB, International Mauritania Telecom, the Orange group, Sonatel and Silverlinks for a Europe-to-South-Africa system landing in Mauritania, Senegal, Guinea, Cote d'Ivoire and Nigeria; no cost, contract or in-service date held

subject: infra.connect
name: WACS cable repair logistics
status: Implemented, depot far from the outage zone
milestone: Repair ship sailed from Portland to Abidjan, 2026-07-23
position_end: The cable's spare-fibre depot sits at Brest, far from the stretch between Senegal and Congo where most outages occur, so a repair ship had to sail from Portland to Abidjan
note: the account is an independent subsea-cable analyst's; no consortium statement on repair times or depot siting is held

subject: infra.connect
name: West Africa Peering Forum
milestone: 2026 forum held in Cotonou, 17-18 June 2026
position_end: The 2026 forum drew 281 participants from 23 countries for technical sessions on exchange-point and peering development; the published report records the host country's own exchange point still carrying under 1 Gbps of traffic after nearly ten years, alongside a newly announced second national exchange point with five connected members

subject: infra.store
name: Data-centre capacity gap
milestone: Market brief published May 2025
position_end: About 150MW to 200MW of new capacity — 30 or more large-scale facilities — needed to reach the capacity-to-population ratio of a moderately mature market such as Morocco, on a regional depth of 0.04MW per million people; as at early 2025 the region was the only one on the continent with no established or announced public cloud region from any of the world's five largest cloud providers
note: an analyst brief commissioned by donor partners, whose regional depth figures are the analyst's own estimates

subject: infra.energy

milestone: US$160m approved 24 June 2026

subject: dpi.pay
name: Institutions connected to PI-SPI

subject: dpi.pay
name: Payment institutions licensed in the monetary union
milestone: Central bank list as at 28 February 2026

subject: dpi.pay

position_end: In service across the eight member states, free for person-to-person transfers, with banks and mobile money interconnected since May 2026

subject: dpi.pay

position_end: In force since 2015: the conditions and procedures under which electronic-money issuers may operate in the member states of the monetary union
note: The instrument the union’s e-money account figures are reported against.

subject: dpi.pay
name: UEMOA Regulation 15/2002/CM on payment systems
milestone: Adopted 19 September 2002
position_end: The founding regional act for payment systems across the monetary union: it sets the legal basis for electronic signatures and certification, makes bank account access mandatory, promotes scriptural payment instruments, and governs netting, settlement finality and the cheque regime - the frame under which the union's later instant-payment and electronic-money instruments sit

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union electronic money and large-microfinance position
milestone: Union e-money outstandings CFAF 1,923.2 billion at 31 December 2025
position_end: Union-wide electronic-money outstandings rose 35.2 per cent to CFAF 1,923.2 billion at 31 December 2025 and electronic-money accounts reached 172.9 million, of which only 60.6 million, 35.1 per cent, were active. Senegal held 29.7 per cent of outstandings and 26.5 per cent of large-microfinance assets, leading on both, with CFAF 1,234.3 billion of microfinance assets ahead of Cote d'Ivoire's CFAF 1,226.7 billion and Burkina Faso's CFAF 889.4 billion, the three together holding 71.9 per cent of the union's large-institution assets; Senegal hosts 81 large institutions against Burkina Faso's 50, Togo's 47 and Cote d'Ivoire's 43
note: the active-account share is the figure that qualifies the rest: nearly two thirds of the union's electronic-money accounts are dormant, and the banking commission's own report is relayed through a press account rather than held directly

subject: dpi.pay
name: Union instruction on payment services
milestone: Instruction 001-01-2024 issued by the central bank governor, 23 January 2024
position_end: The union-wide regulatory instrument for payment services, made under the monetary union treaty and the uniform banking, microfinance and anti-money-laundering laws, governing payment services including electronic-money institutions and mobile payment services
note: the instruction text is held; no licensing or supervisory count under it is; the base holds this one instruction as two records, dated 2024-01-01 and 2024-01-23; the instruction's own date is the latter and this row now carries it

subject: dpi.pay
name: Users connected to PI-SPI
position_end: 30 million connected users and one million transactions worth 110 billion FCFA in under ten months
note: The transaction count is the platform's cumulative total since launch

subject: dpi.mis
name: ASRII Digital Platform
milestone: Four-day ECOWAS Commission training closed at Abuja, 7 August 2026
position_end: Twenty core participants trained across the Commission's directorates with the Directorate of Research and Statistics named as single focal point; the platform is to replace manual collection with submission, validation, automated computation of integration scores and dissemination, and is to be used to evaluate member states' policy implementation and track commitments across sectors. No integration score has been published (2026-08)
note: The African Union Commission's harmonised framework for measuring regional integration across political, economic, infrastructure and human and social pillars, developed with the regional economic communities, UNECA and the African Development Bank. At the closing the Secretary General called for a centralised database of the status, amendments and implications of all regional legal protocols, and for a blueprint for regional data management; the Commission holds neither.

subject: dpi.mis
name: Digital monitoring platform for the continental demographic dividend roadmap
milestone: Regional technical validation convened for 7-9 September 2026
position_end: The Economic Commission for Africa's subregional office and the United Nations Population Fund, with the Ivorian planning and development ministry through its national population office, convened a regional technical validation and operationalisation of a digital monitoring platform for the continental roadmap on harnessing the demographic dividend, from 7 to 9 September 2026 in Abidjan
note: a validation meeting announced rather than reported: no platform description, data source, host institution, indicator set or country coverage is stated

subject: dpi.govtech
name: Strengthening Tax Administration Capacity Project
milestone: Grant agreement signed by 2026-03-11; project launched 2026-08-18
position_end: A regional tax administration forum project financed by a US$5.52m grant from a development fund's transition support facility, with implementation running to 30 July 2030 under a forum-hosted project implementation unit and a multi-stakeholder steering committee
note: the financier's own announcement puts the grant at US$5.52m from the transition support facility and dates the agreement to on or before 2026-03-11, against the 4 million units of account reported as about US$5.3m at the launch five months later; the beneficiary countries are named in the reporting but the project's digital component, its component allocations and its results framework are not itemised anywhere published

subject: tech.ai
name: ECOWAS Regional AI Governance Framework
milestone: Resolved at the Lagos thematic dialogue, 2026-01-22
position_end: Resolved to be developed, citing algorithmic bias, labour displacement and information disorder; no draft, drafting body or date held in the six months since; a four-country comparative study presented on 2026-08-10 found none of Benin, Senegal, Cote d'Ivoire or Burkina Faso holds AI-specific legislation in force or in draft, rating Cote d'Ivoire's strategy the most advanced of the four on inclusion and data governance and finding Burkina Faso's data-protection law the only one to name AI-based processing
sources: 2026-08-10-grain-west-africa-ai-governance-comparative-study|2026-01-24 ECOWAS Adopts Digital Roadmap; Targets Unified Single Market and AI Governance for West Africa

subject: tech.ai
name: Francophone West African AI governance guidelines
milestone: Adopted by six states and submitted to the UN governance dialogue, 2026-07-06
position_end: Adopted by Benin, Burkina Faso, Cote d'Ivoire, Guinea, Mali and Senegal; advisory, complementing national strategies rather than replacing them
note: Convened by Niyel, an advocacy organisation, and not by a regional body

subject: tech.innovate
name: ECOWAS Startup Awards
milestone: Second edition launched, announced Abuja 2026-08-17
position_end: A second edition launched by the Commission's private sector and industry directorate, offering scaling technology-led businesses managerial training, venture funding and cross-border expansion support within the continental free trade area; no prize fund, entry deadline, cohort size or outcome from the first edition is published
note: a launch announcement at a press briefing; the awards' own rules and the first edition's results are not held

subject: capacity.training
name: BCEAO/COFEB certifying programme in digital finance
milestone: Fourth edition opened, applications closing 2026-08-25
position_end: In its fourth edition, run by the monetary union's central bank training centre with Luxembourg's House of Training-ATTF: four modules over about nine months and 84 hours, aimed at senior staff of credit institutions, e-money issuers and microfinance institutions, one candidate per institution, participation fees of FCFA 1.2m, an 80% pass mark per module and a final project defended before a jury at Dakar
note: the brochure carries no publication date beyond 'Edition 2026' and is dated from the server's own header; no cohort size or completion figures for the earlier three editions are published

subject: capacity.training
name: Cybersecurity professionals certified as SIM3 auditors
position_end: 38 professionals from member states and partner institutions trained at Lomé, 4 to 6 August 2026, to assess the maturity of national computer security incident response teams (2026-08)
note: The Security Incident Management Maturity Model is owned by the Open CSIRT Foundation, which delivered the training; hosted by Cyber Defense Africa, operator of Togo's CERT.tg. The Commission states a further aim of a sustainable pool of West African trainers.

subject: capacity.training
name: EU-ECOWAS EPSG support for fact-checking platforms
milestone: Nigerian beneficiaries selected, reported 2026-07-31
position_end: Two Nigerian organisations selected for in-kind technical support covering digital infrastructure, cybersecurity and verification systems, with training in AI, digital investigations and deepfake detection, and admission to a regional cross-border verification network; no amount, duration or start date is stated
note: Activity 3.1.6a(1), implemented by FIAP with FactCheckAfrica

subject: include.access
name: Open e-money accounts in the UEMOA
position_end: 248,710,918 accounts (2024-12-31), of which 76,863,533 active, an activity rate of 30.9%
note: The central bank's own report, published January 2026 with data to 31 December 2024

subject: data.statistics
name: ECOMAC (ECOWAS Multilateral Surveillance Mechanism database)
milestone: Constituted by Council Regulation C/REG.30/12/07, in official journal 52 of 2008-01-01
position_end: The database of the bloc's multilateral surveillance mechanism, constituted by a statistical and computer protocol adopted by the Council of Ministers in December 2007: thirteen Excel tables on a quarterly update cadence with stated deadlines, and supervision divided between the monetary union's commission and central bank, the West African Monetary Agency and the West African Monetary Institute; no later amendment and no operational report is held
note: a 2007 instrument acquired in 2026 and the only published documentation of the database the acquisition pass could reach; the companion ECOBASE database has none

subject: data.statistics
name: ECOWAS regional statistical methodological guides
milestone: Second Abidjan operationalisation workshop, 18-22 August 2026
position_start: The Regional Statistical Programme 2023-2027 under implementation, with no adopted methodological guide held
position_end: Regional methodological guides in use, with a second Abidjan workshop training national coordination and economic policy committee members to operationalise the common regional frameworks for compiling and publishing macroeconomic statistics, reviewing the two regional databases and the harmonisation of member states' 2000-2025 national statistics for multilateral surveillance

subject: data.statistics
name: ECOWAS Statistical Policy and Regional Statistical Programme 2023-2027

subject: data.statistics
name: Migration and macroeconomic data harmonisation
milestone: Two regional workshops held at Abidjan, 18-22 August 2026
position_end: Two regional statistics workshops convened at Abidjan on 18-22 August 2026 under the Commission's research and statistics directorate and its harmonisation project: the sixth Regional Coordination Meeting, which reviewed and validated the third edition of the Regional Report on International Migration in West Africa, and a capacity-building session for national committees on compiling macroeconomic statistics for the Convergence and Macroeconomic Stability Pact; participants also took up updates to the regional macroeconomic and statistical databases and harmonisation of national series for 2000-2025

subject: geopol.china
name: China-aid ECOWAS Headquarters Building
milestone: Handed over at Abuja, 2026-04-28
position_end: Handed over to the Commission, the second international-organisation office complex China has built in Africa; China describes cooperation extending into the digital economy and names no digital programme, figure or instrument, and the Commission's own release names no digital component
note: Both accounts held are China's own; nothing on file states who provisions the building's ICT and network layer
